Chapter 02 — The House

Vision. Foundation.Build. Reveal.Ownership.

The House That Andile Built is the hero media property: a real build, documented from the first plan to the keys — and the platform he owns at the end of it.

Stage status is published as the build progresses. Nothing on this page claims a stage is complete until it is.

  1. 01 · Vision

    It starts as an idea on paper.

    Plans, references and the decision to build something that belongs to him — on camera, from the first sketch.

  2. 02 · Foundation

    Materials, choices, consequences.

    Every material, fitting and trade decision is a scene. The category partners live here, inside the work rather than beside it.

  3. 03 · Build

    Transparent, on site, in progress.

    The build is shown as it happens — the people, the problems and the fixes — so the audience earns the reveal with him.

  4. 04 · Reveal

    The moment the audience has been waiting for.

    Milestones become appointment viewing. The reveal is the payoff the weekly cadence builds toward.

  5. 05 · Ownership

    The house, the show, the audience.

    What is built stays built. The series, the audience relationship and the IP are his to keep and extend.

Chapter 03 — The Flagship

The Flagship

The House That Andile Built

The build series, professionalised into appointment viewing. A fixed weekly cadence, a format the audience learns, and an edit that treats the house like the main character.

Watch the Flagship

  • 01

    Weekly production cadence

    A fixed weekly release rhythm so the build becomes appointment viewing rather than occasional posting.

  • 02

    Format bible

    One document that fixes the structure, tone, segments and rules of the show, so every episode is recognisably the same series.

  • 03

    Recurring segments

    Repeatable segments the audience learns to expect — and that partners can attach to without interrupting the story.

  • 04

    Milestones

    Build milestones mark the season's shape and give the series natural moments to promote, sponsor and celebrate.

  • 05

    Human subplots

    The people around the build — trades, advisers, family where approved — carry the story between milestones.

  • 06

    Cinematic edit

    Long-form episodes cut with the care of broadcast television: considered pacing, grade and sound.

  • 07

    Short-form multiplier

    Each shoot yields clips, vertical edits and milestone moments for every platform, multiplying reach from one production day.

Episodes

Titles, dates and video appear as each edit is approved. Drag, swipe or use the arrows.

Short-form multiplier

One shoot.Many stories.

Every shoot is planned for the hero episode and for everything cut from it: short clips, vertical edits and milestone moments for each platform. Examples show the shape, not published clips.

Ownership

He keeps the show.He keeps the audience.He keeps the IP.

LegacyLeverage is the production and commercial engine, not the owner.

The 90-day pilot

Ninety daysto prove it.

A proving period in three phases of thirty days: stabilise the flagship, package and pitch it, then extend and formalise.

Start the Pilot

  1. Days 01–30

    Phase 1: Stabilise

    • Clear publishing backlog
    • Set format bible
    • Set calendar
    • Launch short-form multiplier

  2. Days 31–60

    Phase 2: Package + Pitch

    • Sponsor deck / rate card
    • Hardware anchor
    • Finance / automotive outreach

  3. Days 61–90

    Phase 3: Extend + Formalise

    • Pilot second format
    • Shared scorecard
    • Co-production terms
